research_question: Does a connectivity/contiguity-inspired allocator reduce unnecessary shared corridors between robots and clots while respecting clot capacity, compared to the nearest and flow_spread baselines?
main_variable: Task allocation rule only: connectivity_aware allocator vs nearest / flow_spread baselines. The allocator emits targets; the final 3D action remains Direct Local GAT-MAPPO output.
reference: C2-Explorer connectivity/contiguity concept adapted to vascular tasks. Its communication-connectivity constraint has no vascular counterpart and is replaced by corridor overlap. This is an adaptation, not an implementation of C2-Explorer.

cost_terms.geodesic_distance: along-vessel travel, normalized by total arclength
cost_terms.path_overlap: fraction of a candidate corridor already used by previously assigned routes
cost_terms.edge_congestion: penalty for edges used by more than one assigned route (first trunk user is free)
cost_terms.flow_cost: fraction of local flow opposing the route direction
cost_terms.switching_penalty: cost of abandoning the robot's previous target
cost_terms.clot_capacity: soft overflow beyond the env's lysis saturation (4 robots), hard respect while an unsaturated clot exists

solver: greedy sequential allocation in increasing geodesic-distance order (overlap couples rows, so a global Hungarian assignment is not applicable); deterministic
application: env.set_task_assignments / vector set_task_assignments override the nearest-clot rule with a live-clot guard; auto-reset invalidates stale rows; planner can also provide corridor hints from the route next-hop field

measured.protocol: 14 anatomical scenarios x 20 episodes, 8 robots, 3 clots, seed 3000+
measured.note: connectivity_aware beats nearest on 14/14 scenarios and flow_spread on 8/14; single-episode snapshot (5 robots): 1.653 vs 1.649 vs 1.959

validation.pytest: tests/test_connectivity_allocator.py: capacity respected, single-clot totality, overlap <= nearest everywhere and <= flow_spread*1.02 on average, switching stability, dispatch validation, vector env override

performance_claim: none on episode success: allocator behaviour is measured on corridor overlap only; closed-loop success requires new training/evaluation runs
